newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania ratifies key treaty with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Romania ratifies key treaty with Ukraine.

text.p: Romania's parliament on Monday endorsed a key treaty settling old rifts over borders and minorities with neighbouring Ukraine.
Parliament's upper Senate voted 60-49, with three abstentions, to ratify the treaty, which reformist President Emil Constantinescu and his Ukrainian opposite number Leonid Kuchma signed last month.
Romania's leftists, who lost their seven-year grip on power in 1996 elections, voted against the pact as did nationalists, now a small minority in a parliament dominated by centrists.
The pact, which the lower Chamber of Deputies had also passed two weeks ago, has to be promulgated by the president before taking effect.

Addressing the Senate after Monday's vote, Foreign Minister Adrian Severin called the treaty "a major contribution to regional security", saying it paved the way for building "special relations" between the two countries.

Ukraine's ambassador to Bucharest hailed Monday's vote as a "historic moment" in bilateral ties. "It is the victory of common sense and the triumph of European values," ambassador Olsksander Cealii told Reuters.
Bucharest dropped its previous insistence that Kiev should atone in the treaty text for the 1939 Soviet-Nazi pact under which Moscow annexed Romanian lands now part of modern Ukraine.

Negotiators have agreed to leave unsolved issues -- including definition of Black Sea borders in areas which both countries believe are rich in oil and gas deposits -- to be settled as part of separate accords.

Romania signed a similar deal patching rifts with Hungary last year, to boost its chances of getting invited to join NATO, alongside favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, when the alliance announces its first eastward expansion at an alliance summit starting in Madrid on Tuesday.
